references.text: Jacob concluded that Joseph had been torn apart by a wild animal, which explains his desperate fear of losing his only remaining son from Rachel, Benjamin.
Jacob refused to be comforted and said he would go down to the realm of the dead in mourning over Joseph—the same expression about bringing gray hair down to Sheol in sorrow.
Jacob finally relents and sends Benjamin to Egypt but commits himself to God Almighty with a prayer for mercy, showing his deep fear of loss.
Judah recounts to Joseph how their father expressed fear of losing Benjamin and notes that Rachel's one son is already gone.
Judah explains that if Benjamin does not return, their father will die—'his gray hair will be brought down to the realm of the dead in sorrow'—almost identical wording to Jacob's own words.
Judah uses the same wording as Jacob in 42:38 to demonstrate that he has learned from the past and is willing to sacrifice himself.
Judah's concern for his father's 'calamity' in 44:34 is the direct fulfillment of the fear Jacob expressed in 42:38.
